title: Приступ радикулита и бездомный котёнок  (A Bout of Sciatica and a Stray Kitten)

segments.t: During their second morning run in the park, Chef Barinov is on the verge of collapsing when Elena suddenly throws her back out and cannot move an inch. Meanwhile back at the apartment, Max and Kostya hatch a clever plan using a stray kitten to appeal to Nastya's soft heart.
Не могу ни туда, ни сюда.
Вы меня не шевелите, я сама, ладно?
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'You got here fast.' Rodion conveys a candid footing right away, joining "bystro" ("quickly") to "zhe" ("but, after all") so every word pulls its weight.
'What is wrong with you?' Max inquires openly without holding back, anchoring the Russian line on "chto" ("what") and "vami" ("you") without extra filler.
'What happened to your back?' Rodion inquires pointedly toward Max here, pairing "spinoy" ("back") with "chto" ("what") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'I cannot move.' Max offers a pointed rhythm in front of Rodion, anchoring the Russian line on "mogu" ("can") and "ne" ("not") without extra filler.
Не могу ни туда, ни сюда.
'I cannot move forward or backward.' Rodion adopts a thoughtful rhythm in the conversation, anchoring the Russian line on "mogu" ("can") and "tuda" ("there") without extra filler.
'Hold on, stop, stop.' Max strikes a measured view in their talk, putting all the weight on "stoyte" ("stop, wait") so the reply lands immediately.
'Wait, hold still.' Rodion projects a measured course in the scene, putting all the weight on "stoyte" ("stop, wait") so the reply lands immediately.
Вы меня не шевелите, я сама, ладно?
'Do not move me, I will try by myself, okay?' Nastya checks decisively to make the point, putting "shevelite" ("to move, stir") alongside "vy" ("you") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'I can do it myself.' Nastya establishes a pointed note across the room, weaving "ya" ("I") together with "sama" ("myself, on my own") just the way native speakers do.
'Bless you.' Max favors an earnest style in the room, leaning on "budte" ("be") before closing the thought with "zdorovy" ("healthy, huge").
'Rodion Sergeyevich, what happened?' Nastya inquires openly during the talk, anchoring the Russian line on "sluchilos" ("happened") and "rodion" ("Rodion") without extra filler.
'Are you feeling worse?' Max queries wryly as they speak, anchoring the Russian line on "khuzhe" ("worse") and "vam" ("you") without extra filler.
'What a sweet little kitten.' Rodion establishes a thoughtful tack in front of Max, putting "malyshka" ("sweetheart") alongside "khoroshiy" ("good") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Не могу ни туда, ни сюда.
Вы меня не шевелите, я сама, ладно?
That wraps up this scene as during their second morning jog in the park, Elena throws her back out when she bends down, and at the restaurant Max hatches a plan using a stray kitten. Until next time!
